EU welcomes Abu Dhabi talks while preparing 22nd package of sanctions against Russia — EC
articles.summary: According to EC President Ursula von der Leyen, the EU would support Ukraine "be it in wartime or be it in peacetime"
articles.body: LONDON, November 12. /TASS/. The European Union welcomes the talks in Abu Dhabi while simultaneously preparing its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said upon arriving in Dublin for the European Political Community summit. "I very much welcome the peace talks in Abu Dhabi," von der Leyen said, adding that the EU would support Ukraine "be it in wartime or be it in peacetime." Von der Leyen also said that, allegedly, European countries "were represented." At the same time, she emphasized that the EU was "preparing the 22nd sanctions package [against Russia]," as well as "a proposal on how to cover the financial needs of Ukraine in 2027," which it intends to present "before the next European Council," scheduled for November 26-27 in Brussels. Russia, the United States and Ukraine held talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11. The first round of consultations lasted four and a half hours, including a 40-minute break, on November 10, followed by a session that lasted about two hours on November 11. Presidential Aide Vladimir Medinsky led the Russian delegation, while Foreign Intelligence Service chief Rustem Umerov headed the Ukrainian delegation. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe Alexus Grynkewich and UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, were also present at the negotiating table when the talks began. Despite statements from French officials, no Europeans attended the meeting. Medinsky revealed that, at the talks, Russia and Ukraine coordinated a major POW exchange, saying that its parameters will be made public soon. He also noted that the theme of the European security system was central to the Abu Dhabi meeting and that the sides found common ground on some aspects of it.

Entire agenda covered in Abu Dhabi, details of talks to stay undisclosed — Russian MFA
articles.summary: All the tools suitable for seeking solutions were used, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov undercored
articles.body: MOSCOW, November 12. /TASS/. The delegations of Russia, the United States and Ukraine discussed the entire agenda in detail during talks in Abu Dhabi, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov assured, but declined to disclose any details. "The entire agenda was thoroughly discussed in full in various formats during meetings, including bilateral meetings between the delegations, in smaller groups and at plenary sessions. Everything was covered. All the tools suitable for seeking solutions were used," the diplomat told RT. "There should be no doubt about that," Ryabkov, who was part of the Russian delegation at this week’s talks in Abu Dhabi, emphasized. The Russian deputy foreign minister declined to say whether territorial issues had been discussed. "The contents of the talks are not subject to disclosure," he explained.

Four grizzly bears killed Canadian mother and daughter, authorities say
articles.summary: DNA testing showed that a mother bear and her three cubs attacked and killed Jennifer Balcarras and Selah Reed in British Columbia last week, authorities said.
articles.body: A grizzly bear and her three cubs were behind the attack that killed two women in British Columbia this month, Canadian authorities said. Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter Selah Reed, 20, were found dead in Bella Coola earlier this month. Officials captured and assessed local bears, and determined via DNA testing that the four bears were “all actively involved” in the attack, Inspector Jeff Tyre of the British Columbia Conservation Officer Service told an online briefing Tuesday. The mother bear was in her teens, while the three cubs had all been born in the past year, Tyre said. He added that the bears were killed to protect the public, because bears involved in fatal attacks on humans “cannot be rehabilitated or relocated.” “Our investigation also found that this attack likely involve predatory behavior, which I can tell you is very rare,” Tyre said. “That is to say, we don’t know how it started, but we know how it ended.” Terry Webber, chief administrative officer for the Nuxalk Nation, said the incident was “deeply re-triggering for our community ,” following a separate grizzly attack on a school group in the same area last year.
